# CPU tensor resize oracle

Generated by `python3 scripts/mm/gen_gemma4_resize_golden.py`, never by C++.
Torch 2.11.0+cu130, git 70d99e998b4955e0049d13a98d77ae1b14db1f45;
CPU only, two threads, uint8 HWC -> 1CHW -> interpolate(bicubic,
antialias=True, align_corners=False) -> HWC bytes. No GPU or weights.
The generator refuses a different Torch revision. Files are uncompressed RGB
outputs; dimensions, FNV hashes and input patterns are in the generator and
`gemma4_resize_golden.inc`. Tests compare every output scalar to these bytes,
not just hashes, and check the production tower input boundary.

Transformers a08ace4bbd97e721c98751deec37d87b026acadc
Gemma4ImageProcessor.aspect_ratio_preserving_resize calls torchvision v2 resize.
Qualified torchvision 0.26.0, commit 336d36e8db990a905498c73933e35231876e28bc,
transforms/v2/functional/_geometry.py:259-340 preserves CPU bicubic uint8 and
calls the same interpolate operator. It does not cast to float and round on
this arm. Torchvision itself is not installed/executed; this is source-qualified
ATen execution, not full HF processor execution. No historical golden's Torch
version is implied. The paired 0.26/2.11 behavior is explicitly pinned here.

ATen native/cpu/UpSampleKernel.cpp at the Torch commit: clipped Keys -0.5
support, double normalized coefficients, per-axis precision chosen from maximum
positive weight, signed half-away int16 coefficient rounding. AA uint8 dispatch
uses AVX for <=4 channels where compiled, otherwise generic separable uint8.
Horizontal and vertical stages each add half, arithmetic shift, saturate uint8.
UpSampleKernelAVXAntialias.h confirms the SIMD rounding/saturation. Shared
Pillow's fixed 22-bit coefficients differ and are deliberately not reused.

Source SHA256:
- torchvision _geometry.py: 52b0edcfa5ebc7cdb596626c3f26e06695a5ea9e95e43bdfc33404bb8dcc0373
- UpSampleKernel.cpp: 3ccfb91f9782362fe2794a25c372f19477d4c568a54351100e430e2470feb234
- UpSampleKernelAVXAntialias.h: 51a3ce1949aba337113becae2b398510be7adfe0a712d61c07c78ac5f8905668

Nine cases cover all five budgets, noninteger up/downscale, hard step edges
and ramp discontinuities (overshoot/rounding/clipping), asymmetric shapes,
1x65536 and 65536x1 and single-axis resizing. Original identity cases remain.
Full processor, prompt/template, device BF16, vision inference and serving
remain pending. This is bounded decoded RGB CPU coverage only.
